title: Weak association is detected after localization at a prime
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, and p a prime ideal of R. Let R_p and M_p denote localization at p [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The following are equivalent: (1) p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of M; (2) the extended prime p R_p is minimal among the prime ideals containing the annihilator of some element of the localized module M_p; (3) M_p contains an element whose annihilator has radical p R_p.

proof.text: For any m in M and s outside p, identify Ann_{R_p}(m/s) with Ann_R(m) R_p. Write a scalar as r/t. The localized scalar kills m/s exactly when some u outside p kills rm; equivalently ur belongs to Ann_R(m), which is exactly the membership criterion for r/t in the extended ideal. The private proved helper colon_localized_mk implements this denominator calculation using IsLocalizedModule.mk'_smul_mk', IsLocalizedModule.mk'_eq_zero' and IsLocalization.mk'_mem_map_algebraMap_iff. The prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], in Mathlib's IsLocalization.minimalPrimes_map, identifies minimal primes over the extended annihilator with minimal primes over Ann_R(m) after contraction. The extension of p contracts to p, by map_eq_maximalIdeal and under_maximalIdeal. Thus p R_p is minimal over the annihilator of m/s if and only if p is minimal over Ann_R(m). Passing between witnesses uses m/1 in one direction and IsLocalizedModule.mk'_surjective in the other. This proves (1) iff (2).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.2, tag 0566, annihilator calculation and localization correspondence

proof.text: Assume (2) with witness x=m/s. By the equivalence established for each fraction in step 1, p is minimal over Ann_R(m). Apply IsLocalization.AtPrime.radical_map_of_mem_minimalPrimes: the radical of Ann_R(m) R_p is p R_p, since localization prime correspondence leaves p R_p as the unique prime over that extended annihilator. Rewrite the extended annihilator using colon_localized_mk. This gives (3) with the same witness.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.66.2, tag 0566, proof of (2) implies (3)

proof.text: Assume (3), witnessed by x, with radical of its annihilator equal to p R_p. Minimal primes over an ideal equal minimal primes over its radical (Ideal.radical_minimalPrimes). Since p R_p is prime, its minimal primes form the singleton containing itself (Ideal.minimalPrimes_eq_subsingleton_self). Therefore p R_p is minimal over the annihilator of x, proving (2).

lean.statement: theorem weakly_associated_atPrime_iff {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] : ((∃ m : M, p ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule R M).colon {m}).minimalPrimes) ↔ (∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).minimalPrimes)) ∧ ((∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∈ ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).minimalPrimes) ↔ (∃ x : LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, ((⊥ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M)).colon {x}).radical = p.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p))))

reviewed_lean.note: CommRing R, AddCommGroup/Module M, p prime (no extra hyps); R_p=Localization.AtPrime p, M_p=LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M, pR_p=p.map algebraMap; (1) colon-{m} minimalPrimes over R, (2) same over R_p for x in M_p, (3) radical of R_p-annihilator = pR_p; (1<->2)&(2<->3); L colon convention (Ideal.WeakAss ring-only, not applicable); Mathlib-only imports; docstring = node's 3 steps
